differences.what: B's tones never reach white: its brightest pixel is luma 236 (p99 227, against 244 in A), so the whole frame looks veiled and the white speaker bodies read light grey (median 214) instead of white (A 232, only 0.2% clipped)
The same capped white point makes the right speaker body look dull grey in B (212 against 231 in A), so it stands out less from the wall
The left 'earmilk' wordmark is clean white and crisp in A (p95 249, edge step 142). In B it is grey and soft (p95 221, step 97), like faded print
The right 'earmilk' wordmark is crisper and whiter in A; in B it looks soft and greyish
On the nutrition panel, A's header and thick rules are crisp and neutral black (luma 36). In B they are lighter (53) with a brown cast on the top rule, and the type is softer
The red gable gloss and the highlights on the waveguide rim are better defined in A, and the gable meets the white body on a clean line. B's gables look flatter and duller
A shows sharpening halos: a 1px white overshoot (254 against 244 on the baffle) and a dark undershoot ring around the woofer surrounds. B's edge transitions are clean
A has a faint light fringe along the gable outline where it meets the wall, also from sharpening. B's edge is clean
The turntable's platter rim and start button have brighter, livelier chrome highlights in A (about 2.5% of the rim area clips, which reads as natural specular). B's chrome is greyish and flat
The wall, mat and artwork look airy and warm in A. In B the same areas look dingy grey (wall luma 200 against 218)
The dried stems are darker and crisper against the wall in A, and softer and washed out in B. Minor
